title: Returnship Launch — 60-Day Reintegration Playbook
content:
Executive summary:

This playbook outlines a return-to-work (returnship) hiring and onboarding program designed for experienced professionals re-entering the workforce after extended career breaks (6+ months). The goal is to create an efficient, low-friction hiring funnel, an interview rubric that accounts for non-linear career trajectories, and a 60-day reintegration checklist that accelerates ramp while providing supportive accommodations.

Goals and success criteria:
- Hire 8 technical contributors and 4 product/generalist hires in Q2 2025 into a 6–12 month paid returnship cohort.
- 90-day retention target for cohort: 85% or higher.
- Ramp metric: contributors should achieve 50% core productivity by day 60 (measured by task throughput + mentor assessment).
- Candidate experience NPS target: +40.

Program principles (how we evaluate design decisions):
- Strength-based assessment: test for current skills and demonstrable problem solving, not penalizing gaps due to time away.
- Flexible logistics: offer asynchronous options, condensed interview schedules, and generous scheduling windows.
- Support-first onboarding: buddy/mentor pairing, clear 30/60 day milestones, and explicit re-skilling time built into schedule.

Candidate profile and role families targeted:
- SWE (backend, infra, inference-serving): IC2–IC3 equivalent; focus on systems thinking, debugging, language model serving familiarity preferred but not required.
- Product + PM generalists: product sense, cross-team communication, stakeholder management.
- Data & ML ops: basic pipeline knowledge, telemetry and incident triage.

Timeline (high level):
- Week 0: Launch job postings + internal nominations + outreach to return-to-work partners.
- Weeks 1–4: Screen and interview first wave (target 40 screens -> 12 offers).
- Weeks 5–8: Offer negotiation + cohort onboarding prep.
- Day 1: Cohort orientation.
- Day 30: Interim check-in, adjust pairings and workload.
- Day 60: Formal reintegration review and placement into standard team flow.

Sourcing channels (prioritized):
- Partnerships: Return-to-Work nonprofits and community organizations (WorkRebooted, PathForward, etc.).
- Internal referral drive and alumni outreach.
- Targeted ads on niche boards (veteran returners, parents returning to work).
- Recruiting events: virtual info sessions with hiring managers and returnship alumni.

Screening funnel and time estimates:
- Application review (resume + cover note focused on reentry context) — 3 days.
- 30-minute phone/virtual screen with recruiter — 3–7 days.
- 45–60 minute hiring-manager or technical screen (can be live or take-home) — 7–10 days.
- Final loop (2–3 interviews, 45 min each, can be same day) — 7–14 days.
- Offer — 3 days.

Accommodations and flexibility guidance for interviewers:
- Offer extra time for coding tasks if requested; provide take-home problems as default alternative.
- Allow asynchronous recorded interviews or separate shorter sessions if candidates have childcare/other constraints.
- Avoid penalizing gaps; ask open questions about recent learning or maintenance projects.

Interview rubric (shared across technical and product roles) — one-page synthesis for interviewers: 
- Core competencies (score 1–5): Technical fundamentals, System design (high-level), Problem solving & debugging, Communication & collaboration, Learning agility.
- Context adjustments: When assessing, account for recency of practice. A candidate who demonstrates a clear learning plan and recent practice exercises should score higher on learning agility.
- Red flags (only if present): inability to explain tradeoffs, poor communication in cross-team scenarios, persistent gaps in role-essential fundamentals after a short refresher attempt.

Recruiter phone screen guide (30 min):
- 5 min: Quick intro, explain returnship format and supports.
- 10 min: Role history — focus on last role before break and any relevant activities during break (volunteer, freelance, coursework).
- 10 min: Motivation & logistics — start date flexibility, part-time/full-time preferences, accommodations.
- 5 min: Next steps and Q&A.

Technical screen (45–60 min) — options and sample prompts:
Option A: Live pair-programming (recommended for backend SDE roles)
- Prompt: Given a simplified kv-store API, debug a scenario where cold-start latency spikes under concurrent warmup. Walk through the root cause hypotheses and outline mitigations (caching, batching, backpressure).
Option B: Take-home (48–72 hrs) — smaller scope, non-trivial system reasoning
- Prompt: Implement a small utility to merge tokenized chat histories and compute per-user memory size; include a short note on how you would scale and measure.
Evaluation guidance for both options: prioritize clarity of thought, tradeoff articulation, and incremental testing. A polished but small solution with clear explanation scores higher than a large messy code dump.

Behavioral and product interviews — sample focus areas and questions:
- Collaboration: "Tell me about a time you negotiated scope with a stakeholder under time pressure."
- Learning & comeback story: "What did you do to stay current during your career break? Give one concrete learning artifact (project, repo, course)."
- Impact: "Describe a feature or bugfix you drove from identification to rollout; what was the measurable outcome?"

Scoring matrix (simple):
- 5: Exceptional — clearly exceeds role expectations, strong learning plan and evidence.
- 4: Strong hire — meets core criteria, minor areas to support.
- 3: Hire with support — meets most fundamentals, needs targeted re-skilling.
- 2: Borderline — multiple gaps, not recommended for this cohort.
- 1: No hire — insufficient evidence.
Decision rule: average interviewer score >= 3.5 plus hiring manager sign-off.

Offer & compensation: 
- Competitive salary band aligned to IC2–IC3 market.
- 12-week returnship paid at full salary; conversion to standard role after 12 weeks contingent on reintegration review. Note: program length can be shortened/extended by hiring manager with People Ops approval.

Onboarding — 0–30 days (Orientation + leveling into a team):
- Pre-boarding (1 week before start): send welcome packet with cohort schedule, team readme, and required access checklist. Set up mentor and buddy.
- Day 1 orientation: executive welcome, People Ops brief (benefits, EAP, flexible scheduling), cohort intros.
- Week 1: role-specific tech ramp: dev environment setup, core codebase walkthrough, small starter ticket with mentor shadow.
- Week 2: guided pairing sessions (4 x 2 hour blocks) focused on debugging, testing, and deployment basics.
- Week 3: ownership micro-project (est. 3–5 days) with clear acceptance criteria; mentor support daily standups.
- Week 4: first 1:1 reintegration check: discuss blockers, energy levels, and any accommodations.

Onboarding — 31–60 days (transition & stabilization):
- Day 30 milestones: complete micro-project, demonstrate independent deploy/revert, and pass a mentor-led knowledge check.
- Weeks 5–7: increase scope of tickets; begin participating in planning meetings.
- Day 45: mid-point manager review: performance feedback + career path conversation.
- Day 60: reintegration review with hiring manager + People Ops — decision to convert to standard headcount, extend returnship, or provide additional support.

Mentorship & buddy model:
- Each returnee assigned a mentor (technical lead) and a peer buddy. Expectation: 2–4 hours/week of mentor time for first 8 weeks.
- Weekly 1:1s (mentor) and weekly cohort retro (People Ops facilitated).

Measurement & reporting (dashboard fields to capture):
- Applications, interview-to-offer rate, offer acceptance rate, start rate, 30/60/90 retention, ramp score (mentor assessment), cohort NPS, time-to-ready (days to first independent deploy).

Risks and mitigations:
- Low conversion rate from offers: widen sourcing channels, increase internal referral bonuses for cohort hires.
- Burnout / early attrition: explicit check-ins, flexible hours options, reduce initial workload intensity.
- Manager bandwidth: cap mentors to 2 returnees concurrently; provide small manager stipend for extra coordination.

Budget & headcount ask (Q2 2025):
- Headcount: 12 returnship slots (8 eng, 4 product/ops).
- Estimated FY25 Q2 budget: salary + recruiting + stipends = $360k (approx). Detailed budget in attached sheet (linked artifact).

Next steps (owner = Marisol Vega):
- Finalize job descriptions and approval (due: 2025-02-20).
- Confirm partnerships and schedule first info session (due: 2025-02-28).
- Build recruiting tracker + dashboard (due: 2025-03-05).

Appendix: Quick interviewer cheat-sheet (to paste into calendar invites)
- Remind candidate of returnship intent; ask about any scheduling constraints.
- Focus on learning agility and current thinking rather than total years of continuous practice.
- If candidate requests a take-home, default to providing 48–72 hour window.

Notes to self / loose ideas (working):
- Consider part-time returnship lanes for caregivers who need gradual ramp.
- Offer cohort alumni ambassador program to help source future candidates.
- Partner with a local re-skilling bootcamp for a funded re-onboarding week before Day 1.

End of doc.
